## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Telādi* section constitutes rules 2 through 8 of the Pāṭidesanīya (*Pātidesanīya*) chapter of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. These rules regulate the conduct of fully ordained nuns regarding the solicitation of specific luxury or delicate foodstuffs without being ill—namely oil (*tela*), honey, syrup, fish, meat, milk, and curd [SuttaCentral]. A modern English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
In terms of textual reuse and parallels, the text shares extensive stock phrasing with adjacent Vinaya rules. According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the closest Pali-internal parallels occur in *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pāṭidesanīya* 1, the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya* 39 rule (which similarly governs the requisition of fine foods by monks), the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya* 84 and 85, along with citations across commentary and subcommentary literature such as the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-linguistic matches identified by DharmaNexus align segments of the Pali text with Sanskrit counterparts in the *Prātimokṣasūtra* and *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya*, as well as Tibetan translations in the Kangyur and Tengyur, including the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005), the *Pratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4107), and the *Vinayasūtraṭīkā* (D4120-2) [DharmaNexus].
